newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-ANWAR AND EJAZ BOOST PAKISTAN WITH STAND OF 262.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ANWAR AND EJAZ BOOST PAKISTAN WITH STAND OF 262.

text.p: A 262-run second-wicket partnership between acting captain Saeed Anwar and Ejaz Ahmed put Pakistan in a handsome position over New Zealand at the end of the second day of the second test on Friday.
After dismissing the touring team for 249, the Pakistanis suffered an early blow when opener Zahoor Elahi (2) was caught in the slips off Chris Cairns with only six runs on the board.

But it was a long, long time before the New Zealanders achieved success again as Anwar, leading Pakistan in the absence of the injured Wasim Akram, and Ejaz mixed caution and aggression to hit centuries which took their side to 269 for two at the close.

Each batsman was prepared to wait for the hittable ball and they found plenty from an attack that lacked the accuracy displayed in the first test at Lahore that gave the New Zealanders a rare win in Pakistan.
The Pakistani pair scored their runs together in 268 minutes off 394 balls before Ejaz was adjudged lbw to Cairns for 125, an innings that included 19 fours and a huge six of off-spinner Dipak Patel.
Ominously, Anwar was still there on the close on 130 along with nightwatchman Mushtaq Ahmed, one not out.
It was Mushtaq who had finished off the New Zealanders in the morning session, the leg spinner ending with six for 87 off 30 overs.

He shared the bowling spotlight with test debutant Mohammed Zahid, who ended with four for 64 off 21 overs after removing stubborn New Zealand captain Lee Germon, who was caught behind by Moin Khan for 55, his first test half-century.
Germon had played a major part in taking his side to semi-respectibility after they slumped to 110 for six on the first day, joining Stephen Flemming in an 81-run partnership.
